guide.summary: Lake cruises, Arrowtown history, adventure operators, cafés, dinners and bars around Queenstown, checked against their own websites.
guide.tip: Kiwi Park, the Lakes District Museum, the Kawarau Bungy Centre and Kinross all close on Christmas Day, while Patagonia Chocolates in Arrowtown says it stays open on Christmas Day and Boxing Day.

toolkit.label: Closing days
toolkit.copy: Kiwi Park, the Lakes District Museum, the Kawarau Bungy Centre and Kinross close on Christmas Day. The Winery on Ballarat Street also lists Christmas Day, Easter Friday, Easter Sunday and Anzac Day until 12pm as closures.

toolkit.label: Tickets and booking
toolkit.copy: RealNZ advises booking the TSS Earnslaw in advance because availability is limited, and its booking process does not work in private or incognito browsing. Onsen Hot Pools has released availability up to 30 April 2027.

toolkit.label: Walk-ins
toolkit.copy: Eichardt's Bar at 2 Marine Parade does not take reservations and encourages walk-ins between 11am and 10pm. Fergburger on Shotover Street lists daily hours from 7am to 2.30am.

toolkit.label: Age and height rules
toolkit.copy: The minimum age for AJ Hackett's Kawarau Bridge Bungy is 10, and Ziptrek's Moa and Kea tours are for ages 6 and up. Shotover Jet's daily banner showed a 1.0m minimum height when checked.

guide.dek: Pair a lake cruise or jetboat ride with a half day in Arrowtown, and book cruises and hot pools ahead.
intro: Queenstown's lakefront makes an easy base. From Steamer Wharf at 88 Beach Street, RealNZ runs the TSS Earnslaw across Lake Whakatipu; its page says cruises run regularly throughout the day and advises you to book ahead because availability is limited. The same wharf is the departure point for the Walter Peak Gourmet BBQ, a three and a half to four hour outing with a buffet at the Homestead Restaurant and a farm dog show. Up the hill at 51 Brecon Street, Kiwi Park opens every day with seasonal hours, 9:30am to 6:30pm in summer and 9:30am to 5pm in winter, and closes on Christmas Day.

Arrowtown is worth a half day. The Lakes District Museum at 49 Buckingham Street opens every day from 9am to 5pm and closes on Christmas Day; adult entry is $14 and children under five go free. Its gallery lists an exhibition by Kate Bray from 17 December 2026 to 14 February 2027. At the top end of Buckingham Street, near Bush Creek, the Department of Conservation's Arrowtown Chinese Settlement has a main walk along an old dray track that suits wheelchairs and buggies, though the side tracks do not. Patagonia Chocolates on Ramshaw Lane lists 9am to 6pm daily.

For adrenaline, Shotover Jet leaves from its beach at 3 Arthurs Point Road, and its daily banner showed a 1.0m minimum height when checked. AJ Hackett's Kawarau Bungy Centre on State Highway 6 in Gibbston sets a minimum bungy age of 10 and says it is open daily except Christmas Day. Ziptrek Ecotours books from 45 Camp Street, and its Moa and Kea tours are for ages 6 and up. Further along Arthurs Point Road, Onsen Hot Pools lists 9am to 11pm and has released bookings up to 30 April 2027, so you can plan well ahead.

Food and drink cluster around the bay. Fergburger at 42 Shotover Street lists 7am to 2.30am every day, with Fergbaker next door at number 40 opening from 6am. Bespoke Kitchen on Isle Street serves from 7:30am. Eichardt's Bar at 2 Marine Parade takes no reservations and welcomes walk-ins from 11am to 10pm, and Eichardt's, which holds a MICHELIN Key for 2025 and 2026, opens The Grille daily from 11am. Little Blackwood on Steamer Wharf won Best Bar at the 2026 Hospitality New Zealand Awards. Out in Gibbston, Kinross runs its cellar door from 10am to 5pm.
summaryCards: Start at Steamer Wharf for the TSS Earnslaw, then walk up Brecon Street to Kiwi Park, which opens daily except Christmas Day.
Have breakfast at Bespoke Kitchen on Isle Street from 7:30am, then head to Arrowtown, where the Lakes District Museum opens at 9am every day except Christmas Day.
Book the TSS Earnslaw ahead on RealNZ's site, and check minimum ages: 10 for the Kawarau bungy and 6 for Ziptrek's Moa and Kea tours.

limitations: Website review, not a visit or telephone confirmation. Advertised opening, booking and exhibition details do not guarantee availability. Skyline Queenstown and Coronet Peak returned 403 errors, the QLDC site (Queenstown Gardens) showed a bot check, Rātā and Madam Woo had certificate errors, The Boatshed returned 401, Bardeaux refused the connection, and Remarkables Market, Arrowtown Bakery, Ivy & Lola's, Wolf and Odyssey did not resolve; none of these failures is evidence of closure. Hours were not published on the pages read for Little Blackwood, Blue Kanu, Sherwood, the TSS Earnslaw and Walter Peak. Hours for Yonder and The Winery come from undated pages, and the Cookie Bar page is copyright-dated 2025. Bespoke Kitchen and the Kawarau Bungy Centre show conflicting hours on their own pages. Kiwi Park and the Kawarau Bungy Centre do not give exact dates for their summer and winter hours beyond what is quoted.
